items.summary: Drop virtual buffer attributes with invalid XML names (#20629)
items.fullMessage:
Drop virtual buffer attributes with invalid XML names (#20629)

Fixes #7173

### Summary of the issue:

Malformed markup can make a browser expose accessibility attribute names
that are not valid XML names. For example, `<section
aria-label"almenük">` (note the missing `=`) yields an IA2 attribute
name containing quote characters. NVDA stores virtual buffer fields as
XML markup, so emitting such a name makes expat reject the buffer
content: NVDA plays an error sound and cannot read the affected range in
browse mode.

Minimal test case (from @jcsteh), pasted into the Firefox address bar:

```
data:text/html,<section aria-label"almen%C3%BCk" role="region">test
```

### Description of user facing changes:

Browse mode now reads pages containing this kind of malformed markup
normally; the broken attribute is ignored.

### Description of developer facing changes:

`VBufStorage_fieldNode_t::addAttribute` now rejects attributes whose
names are not valid XML names, returning `false`. This applies to all
virtual buffer backends.

### Description of development approach:

Validation happens once, in `addAttribute`, the attribute map's single
insertion point, so the buffer only ever holds names that are valid in
the XML it serializes to. `isValidXMLAttribName` in
`nvdaHelper/common/xml.h` accepts a conservative ASCII subset of XML
names: the expat build Python ships enforces the stricter XML 1.0 fourth
edition name rules, and every attribute name NVDA's Python code consumes
is ASCII, so anything outside that subset can only be junk from broken
markup. Because only valid names can reach the map,
`generateAttributesForMarkupOpeningTag` now writes stored names directly
and `sanitizeXMLAttribName` is deleted.

Dropping the attribute extends the tradeoff made in #6249, which rewrote
spaces in names to underscores: a readable buffer is worth more than
preserving an attribute nobody can parse. The practical difference is
that a name with invalid characters, such as a localised action name
containing spaces, is now absent from the buffer instead of exposed
under a mangled name. The well-known ASCII names NVDA itself consumes
are unaffected.

An existing XML library was considered and rejected; see the review
discussion below for the survey.

### Testing strategy:

- GitHub Actions for the head commit: build, lint, type checks, unit
tests, and all but two system test jobs pass.
- The two red jobs (`chrome_misc_aria` on windows-2025-vs2026, `l10n` on
windows-2022) each pass on the other OS in the same run, and master is
currently red on two different system test suites, so both look like
known runner flakiness rather than this change.
- Manual: loaded the Firefox test case above; browse mode reads "test"
with no error sound.

### Known issues with pull request:

None in the changed code. Two required system test jobs are red; see
testing strategy.

items.summary: Preserve voice setting support in SynthDriver under automatic profiles
items.fullMessage:
Preserve voice setting support in SynthDriver under automatic profiles

- Override SynthDriver.isSupported() to always report True for the "voice" setting even when Automatic Language Profiles hides voice controls from supportedSettings.
- Ensure NVDA's SynthDriver.loadSettings() initializes the active configured voice via changeVoice(self, voice) instead of passing None.
